title: After-hours NVLink dive & microbatch oddities
content:
Goal: capture quick hypotheses, CLI commands, and triage steps for the NVLink/microbatch p99 regressions observed on ded-rt-03 during the 03/09 overnight window. This is an after-hours scratchpad — rough, prioritized for handoff to morning shift.

Summary of what I saw (03/09 23:30–02:00):
- Sustained p99 token latency from ~95ms baseline -> 175–220ms across short sequences (~64 tokens) on ded-rt-03.
- CPU usage on host low (~15–25%), GPU util ~65%, but NVLink counters show increased remote access stalls.
- KV cache hit rate unchanged; memory pressure reported but not OOM.
- Reproducer: stress with small chat worker + batch_size 1 but many concurrent sessions (~350).

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) NVLink congestion due to unexpected KV cache sharding fallback path when batch size==1 causes cross-GPU fetches more often.
2) CUDA IPC churn from rapid attach/detach when we spawn ephemeral workers under high session churn.
3) Scheduler batching changes earlier this week changed ordering so we get more interleaving across model partitions -> more cross-GPU comm.
4) Thermal clock-throttling (less likely given GPU util moderate, but counters show slight freq dips).

Quick logs/snippets I pulled:
- nvidia-smi topo -m on ded-rt-03 shows one GPU with NVSwitch link quality degraded (error packets ~10/hour).
- /var/log/syslog snippet: "iommu: msgdma timeout" around 2026-03-09T23:47 — needs correlation with kernel ring buffer.
- NVLink perf counters (nvprof equivalent): remote_read_latency spiked for gid 2->5 during the window.

Commands to re-run lightweight repro (safe for night):
- start a controlled harness: ./tools/repro-runner --model redwood-v0.9 --workers 4 --sessions 350 --seq 64 --microbatch 1 --log-sampler 0.05 
- collect counters: sudo perf record -a -g -F 99 -- sleep 30 (not great on prod) -> prefer nvidia-smi dmon and nvml sampling.
- nvlink counters: sudo nvlink_stats --sample-interval 5 --duration 120 --gpus 0,1,2,3 (script in tools/ops/nvlink_stats.sh)

Immediate temp mitigations to try (low-risk):
- pin serving threads so that hot session workers avoid spawning on the problematic GPU (node-level routing change).
- reduce concurrency throttle (soft cap to 260 sessions) for ded-rt-03 via routing rule; see infra/route-rules/rule-rt03.yaml.
- fallback model variant: redwood-v0.9-2gpu-replica (more replication, less cross-gpu KV fetching).

Longer-term experiments to schedule (put in sprint if validated):
- Reproduce with instrumented NVLink counters and a wiretap of the KV fetch path: add per-fetch origin labels and tally cross-gpu fetch rate.
- Add adaptive microbatching heuristic: if cross-gpu fetch rate > X% then prefer larger microbatch or local shard. This intersects with scheduler code in batch_scheduler.rs.
- Add backoff on ephemeral worker attach/detach to reduce CUDA IPC churn (track handles created/sec).

Open action items (who / when):
- Arjun: re-run repro with nvlink_stats + kernel ring buffer attached, capture perf, tag logs. Due: 2026-03-11 AM. (added to RT-789)
- Me (Talia): push a small routing rule to reduce sessions on ded-rt-03 (if infra approves). Due: tonight if ops ok.
- Sofia: review scheduler PR that changed ordering last week (PR #4812) and identify whether batching boundaries changed for microbatch==1. Due: 2026-03-12.

Notes for morning handoff: please include raw nvlink csv, dmesg around 23:30–00:15, and the repro harness stdout. Correlate with cloud provider's host maintenance logs (I saw a maintenance ping around 03/09 22:55 but not sure it's related).

Things I tried (failed / partial):
- Cold restart of the GPU daemon on ded-rt-03 briefly resolved p99 but came back within 12 minutes. Likely symptom not root cause.
- Temp increase microbatch to 4 improved p99 but increased median slightly; customer-facing risk unacceptable long-term.
- Forced affinity to local shards (via experimental flag) reduced cross-gpu reads by ~40% in single-run test.

Quick debugging checklist for whoever picks this up: (tick as you go)
- [ ] Attach nvlink sampling (5s intervals) while running repro harness
- [ ] Capture kernel ring buffer and dmesg window (timestamps)
- [ ] Compare scheduler trace logs (batch boundaries) to see interleaving
- [ ] Check model partition placement metadata for ded-rt-03 (maybe one model got reshuffled)
- [ ] Verify KMS/HSM agent not running heavy ops concurrently (rare, but saw correlation in one run)

Hypotheses to disprove first: thermal throttling (check GPU clocks during spike); NVSwitch hw error (talk to infra to cross-check switch logs). If those are clean -> focus on scheduler/IPC path.

Back-of-envelope numbers to rationalize mitigation cost: dropping concurrency cap 350->260 reduces throughput ~25% but p99 may drop ~30–40% from anecdotal runs. If we can automate adaptive dial we get most of benefit without manual routing rules.

Random notes / brain dump:
- Might be worth adding an "NVLink health" signal to console and alerting if remote_read_latency increases suddenly for a node. Could be a fast signal for routing fallback.
- Consider surfacing per-node microbatch success rate in the console (how often microbatch==1 satisfied without cross-gpu fetch).

Links / pointers:
- scheduler change (PR): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4812
- repro harness: tools/repro-runner README (internal) - doc id: RT-789
- NVLink stats script: tools/ops/nvlink_stats.sh (internal)

Handoff msg to put in Slack (#runtime-nightops):
"Found nvlink/remote-read latency spikes on ded-rt-03 overnight causing microbatch p99 regressions. Lowering session cap and running nvlink sampling now. See users/after-hours-nvlink-dive-talia.json for notes and next steps. Tagging @arjun @sofia for repro + scheduler review."

End of scratchpad.
